source.title: Minimum Viable Specification for a Worldwide Agentic Web
source.author: Cognizant AI Lab

purpose: Authoring source for excerpts embedded with their citations in spec_scout network instructions; not a separately loaded runtime data source. These selected quotations are not the complete specification.

excerpts.topic: Portable resolved network definitions
excerpts.text: Because JSON is a valid HOCON serialization, a site MAY publish an equivalent, fully resolved JSON document for browser loading. The published form MUST preserve the Neuro SAN data model and MUST NOT depend on local includes, environment substitutions, or publisher-only file paths that the Neuro SAN HOCON format affords on server systems.

excerpts.topic: Agent identity, instructions, and callable tools
excerpts.text: Each agent has a unique name within the scope of a single agent network hocon description, a function description, instructions when it uses an LLM, and a list of agents or tools it may call.

excerpts.topic: Callable input and output schemas
excerpts.text: Callable agents and tools expose JSON Schema-compatible inputs. Structured outputs SHOULD also declare schemas.

excerpts.topic: Published instructions are public data
excerpts.text: The minimum interoperable network definition MUST be declarative data. Its published instructions and schemas form a public interoperability surface and MUST NOT be treated as a confidentiality mechanism; reuse remains subject to the publisher’s license and terms.

excerpts.topic: Finite execution limits
excerpts.text: Enforce finite limits on composition depth, agent invocations, remote calls, concurrency, and elapsed execution time. Limits SHOULD be configurable by network, subject to runtime-defined maximums. A runtime MAY detect or prevent cycles when appropriate to its execution model; repeated invocation of the same agent MUST NOT, by itself, be treated as a cycle.

excerpts.topic: Peer network names and site bases
excerpts.text: A peer network is identified by an HTTP or HTTPS URL whose final path component is its published network name. In this version, the runtime treats the preceding path as the site base and retrieves agent-manifest.json from that base.

excerpts.topic: Peers run in the caller with the caller's inference settings
excerpts.text: The caller instantiates the peer network in the caller’s runtime. The peer uses the caller’s active LLM router, model policy, and execution limits. When a user key is active, it is sent only to that router and never to the peer site.

excerpts.topic: Approval before third-party contact
excerpts.text: An interactive runtime MUST provide a consent mechanism governing contact with third-party origins. By default, it MUST identify the external origin and purpose of the contact and obtain the user’s approval before each contact. A runtime MAY support alternative trust policies and consent interfaces, but any relaxation of the default MUST result from an explicit user choice.

excerpts.topic: Exact manifest network matching
excerpts.text: An external-network URL identifies a site base and a requested network name. The runtime retrieves the site’s static agent-manifest.json and selects the entry whose name exactly matches the requested network. If no exact match exists, it MUST fail rather than select another published network.

excerpts.topic: Manifest-relative definition fetch and validation
excerpts.text: The runtime resolves the manifest's hocon value against the peer site base, fetches the referenced network definition, and validates it before execution. The value MAY be a relative path or an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL. This version follows normal browser fetch redirects and relies on browser CORS enforcement; it does not require the final network-definition URL to remain on the manifest's origin.

excerpts.topic: Declarative peer loading does not require publisher code
excerpts.text: A conforming runtime MUST be able to retrieve and instantiate the declarative network definition identified by a peer-network URL. Conformance does not require downloading or executing publisher-supplied code. Cross-origin artifacts MUST be published with appropriate CORS headers.

excerpts.topic: Peer site actions remain on their owning origin
excerpts.text: Cross-origin invocation of site-registered actions is an extension and is not required for MVP conformance. Such actions remain on their owning origin and retain that origin’s authentication and authorization controls.

excerpts.topic: Publisher links and caller-owned overrides
excerpts.text: The publisher owns the default peer-network link bindings in the public links.json. A binding supplied at runtime for an unresolved named peer-network reference is caller-owned and MUST NOT modify the publisher’s file.

excerpts.topic: Credential-free public cross-origin artifacts
excerpts.text: When a browser retrieves a public agent artifact from another origin, the publishing origin MUST permit that retrieval through standard browser cross-origin controls. Public artifact requests MUST NOT include the caller’s private credentials.

excerpts.topic: BYOK keys are disclosed only to the selected router
excerpts.text: When BYOK is active, the key remains in the caller's browser and is attached only to model requests sent to the selected router. A conforming runtime MUST NOT place it in URLs, manifests, agent network specification, prompts, action arguments, traces, analytics, or peer-site requests.

excerpts.topic: Peer router metadata cannot replace the caller's router
excerpts.text: The top site selects the active default or BYOK router. A loaded peer inherits that router; its manifest cannot replace the router or receive a user key. Any router metadata present in a peer manifest is informational during composition and MUST NOT override the caller’s active inference path.

excerpts.topic: Validation does not establish trust in peer instructions
excerpts.text: Peer-network definitions MUST be treated as untrusted input to the caller’s inference model. Although the declarative format prevents those definitions from executing directly as code, publisher-supplied agent instructions can still attempt to manipulate the caller’s model—for example, by overriding caller policies, eliciting information available to the model, or inducing unsafe tool or action calls. Schema validation and coded-tool sandboxing do not establish trust in the peer network or its publisher.

excerpts.topic: Private context is deny-by-default, unlike delegated request text
excerpts.text: Private-context fields MUST NOT pass from one network invocation to another by default. Only explicitly named fields MAY be forwarded under an applicable allow rule. The delegated request text is ordinary input to the destination network and is not filtered as private context.

excerpts.topic: Unsafe or over-limit invocations must fail visibly
excerpts.text: If a network, tool, or action invocation cannot be safely validated, resolved, or authorized, or exceeds an applicable execution limit, the runtime MUST NOT begin or continue that invocation and MUST NOT represent it as successful. The failure MUST be reported to the invoking network.

excerpts.topic: Interoperability demonstration: approved peer execution
excerpts.text: After user approval, load an exact named network from a second origin and run it locally in the caller's browser.

excerpts.topic: Interoperability demonstration: peer credential and router isolation
excerpts.text: When a user key is active, show that the second site never receives it and cannot change the caller's router.
